title: Sequence-aware SLI bucketing + synthetic failover sim + unified circuit viz
creator: Aditi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current token-level SLI dashboards treat requests as a single distribution and do not account for sequence length, prompt type, or model-variant routing. This hides correlated tail latencies from specific workload slices and makes multi-region failover behavior hard to validate.

Goal: Implement sequence-aware SLI bucketing (by token count and prompt category), add a synthetic failover simulator to exercise circuit-breakers and region routing, and ship a consolidated dashboard that visualizes circuit states, shedding decisions, and per-bucket token-latency SLIs. The dashboard should support on-demand synthetic runs and link back to runbooks/PRs for operator action.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Instrumentation: token-level latency histograms are emitted with labels: sequence_bucket (0-32,33-128,129-512,512+), prompt_type (system/user, chat/complete), model_variant, region, route_id.
2) SLI derivation: SLI calc job produces per-bucket P50/P95/P99 and error rate for each 1m window and exports to alerting backend.
3) Dashboard: a single dashboard shows per-region circuit statuses, active shedding percentage, synthetic traffic run results, and per-bucket latency trends with drilldowns.
4) Synthetic failover sim: A CLI/endpoint can run a configurable scenario (inject region outage, increase load, force model-variant degradation) and the platform emits telemetry and a summary report.
5) Runbook links and rollback checks are present on the dashboard.
6) Observability tests: automated e2e test runs produce predictable telemetry within the pipeline and are added to CI smoke checks.
implementation_plan:
Phase A (2w): Schema changes and metrics plumbing: update runtime telemetry to tag token spans with sequence_bucket and prompt_type; add model_variant and route_id labels. Update exporter to avoid high cardinality by bucketing and sampling policies.
Phase B (1w): SLI derivation job changes: extend aggregation pipeline to compute per-bucket percentiles and error rates and store rollups. Add alerts for sudden P95 climbs in any bucket.
Phase C (2w): Dashboard and simulator: build Grafana dashboard panels and a small synthetic driver service (container) that can run scenarios via the console. Add visualizations for circuit states and shedding events.
Phase D (1w): Runbook integration, e2e tests, and rollout: link dashboards to incident runbooks, add CI smoke for synthetic sim, staged rollout to canary region then all regions.
dashboard_widgets: Widgets planned: 1) Multi-region map with circuit breaker states (Healthy/Degraded/Open) and active shed rate. 2) Heatmap: sequence_bucket x prompt_type P99 latency. 3) Time-series: per-bucket P50/P95/P99 with region overlays. 4) Event timeline: shedding/circuit events with links to traces and logs. 5) Synthetic run summary tile with pass/fail and aggregated deltas vs baseline. 6) Alert panel showing fired rules and suggested actions.
metrics_spec: Emit histogram: runtime.token.latency_ms with labels [sequence_bucket, prompt_type, model_variant, region, route_id]. Use bucket boundaries tuned for expected token timings (1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024). Emit counter: runtime.token.errors with matching labels. Sampling: full capture for p99 analysis in canary and 1% sampling in high-throughput regions with deterministic reservoir for tail analysis.

decisions: Hash route_id to 8-char prefix to control label cardinality.
Reservoir sampling: full capture in canary region, 1% deterministic tail sampling in high-volume regions.
Synthetic sim will run against dedicated synthetic endpoints and will never change live routing tables; failover is simulated by temporarily toggling synthetic backends.
P95 and P99 per-bucket alerts will trigger SRE paging; P50 regressions will create tickets for tracking but not page.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: High-cardinality labels may increase backend costs and query latency. Mitigation: use bucketing + hashed route_id and sampling.
Risk: Synthetic sim accidentally triggers cross-region cascading effects. Mitigation: run sims only on synthetic endpoints and add preflight dry-run checks.
Risk: Alert noise from new per-bucket alerts. Mitigation: start with canary-only alerts, tune thresholds, and apply suppression windows for new alerts.
